Infinite Wealth is the friends we made along the way.

It's an improvement in every aspect from the previous game, save for the story. Aside from Yamai (the new GOAT), almost everything in the plot feels like a leap backwards (not as forgettable as Yakuza 4, but pretty close).

I enjoyed my time with it, but it's one of the worst entries in the series, kinda wish there was a "meh" button.

All the things you liked about Yakuza: Like a Dragon and more. The ability to move characters during combat and position based effects makes this, truly a must play for turn based RPG fans. RGG has also like before has jam packed this game with side activities to experience. 
Arcade classics such as Virtua Fighter and Outrun in addition to Crazy Taxi and Pokemon Snap like activities makes this a great value game. Not to mention the Dondoko Island activity which emulates city building and Animal crossing. 
Highly recommend any franchise veterans and non veterans to try this game.
wihtout a doubt the best turn based combat ive played. Story had some silly moments but still preeetty good.

Story is amazing, game mechanics are a little more fluid than last time! Don't care about the whole NG+ controversy because the bare-bone game is what you want to play. It is a short and sweet experience that will last you short of 100 hours. I would pay for a small extra chapter at the end that it is so good if there was one!

Other than the price and questionable DLC, I really cannot see what people are fussing about with this game. It's perfected in its gameplay and I absolutely enjoy it very much. I also appreciate the fact that they drastically improved on the turn based combat, allowing you to get creative on how and where you wish to approach your enemies from in order to gain the upper hand. I want RGG to correct their pricing and DLC by their next release so I still have faith in that, otherwise amazing game and keep up the good work RGG.

My point. This game is fucking awesome. People giving it a negative review and saying, "awesome game but paywall new game+" are doo doo heads. Yes the tactic is scummy, yes I think it's shitty, but the game is fucking awesome. 70 hours in and I have no idea how much longer I have.

I'm not the biggest RPG/JRPG guy but this one slaps and has quickly become the one I think of the most fondly. It's the epitome of a great sequel, developing the very new, very fresh direction of Y:LAD in almost every way. The combat is better, the side-systems and management minigame are more fun, and overall, it feels like you're always a short walk from engaging with one of the many, many features that interweave. 

Storywise, I wasn't left lacking much but I was also not blown out of the water. It's enjoyable, entertaining, and has plenty of Yakuza charm. That being said, it's always easier to backseat write, but I think this delicate transitional entry in the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series should have had a little more oomph.

Ive finally managed to finish this game. And man, what a ride! I loved every moment of it. The one thing I liked is how Ichiban as a new protagonist is just as likeable as Kiryu Kazuma. The minigames are fun, the rpg mechanics are more refined, giving you more control over the combat. RGG delivers once again. The story drags here and there, but is still very emotionally charged. 4 stars out of 5.

This game is a fantastic experience, simple yet impactful. While the story might not be as deep as some would hope, it harmonizes beautifully with the myriad activities available. The abundance of islands, Sugimon, and free activities enriches the adventure without overshadowing it. Yes, at times the grind can be challenging, but remember, the greater the challenge, the more rewarding the experience.

Though there are some drawbacks, like the paywall behind NG+ and certain QOL issues reminiscent of the first game, these do not eclipse the overall enjoyment. If you loved the previous Like a Dragon title, dive into this one! It expands on the foundation laid before, offering a bigger and often better journey. I wholeheartedly recommend it!

P.S. And it runs great on Steam Deck. One session is approximately 2.5-3h till the battery dies. Almost no visual artefacts and no performance issues.

As a fan of the series for ten years, before it took off, when it seemed like it's status in the west was doomed to die... Playing this game felt like getting closure on all that began there, and finally looking towards the next chapter.

This is the best game I've ever played. It is my new favorite game. I do not think someone who jumped in from Like a Dragon, or even 0, could feel the way I do about this, but that's okay. I also understand this is something of a hot take, that some long term fans are unsatisfied. That's also okay. After it cooled I definitely see faults with the narrative.

But like... I don't care. No other game felt this rewarding towards my investment in the series prior. Things I never thought would get referenced again get referenced heavily. Faces from long ago finally return. It truly feels like a big Farewell to the past, finally letting RGG look towards the future firmly. Sure, it ain't perfect, it's clumsy as hell, but it has more heart than I've seen in any of these games, and that truly is saying a lot. (And, admittedly, 4 and 5 are some of my favorites in the series, and they're way worse about the clumsiness. I think it's just part of the charm).

Thank you, for everything you've done for me the past ten years. I'm thrilled to see where you go.

I can't recommend this game enough with words, but I will try... The sheer depth of activities and things to do within the game, are mind blowing. Want to make animal friends around Hawaii? Want to play a game of SNAP on the various trolleys around the city? Want to play a CRAZY taxi delivery game? Want to restore and build a resort welcoming various guests and fulfilling their requests to maximize profits? Want to collect various thugs around town and force them to battle in an underground arena on your quest for fame and glory? Have you played Persona and want to enjoy crawling through a dungeon with the rewards getting better the further you go? Want to do it all with lovable characters and an interesting story? Look no further, if you like games, this is THE game for you. So many games within the game, and they are all incredibly well done. I am never bored, and there is always something interesting to do. And of course, as with all Yakuza games there is KIRYU CHANNNNNNNNNNN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Its good. Not "Like a Dragon good" but fun at least. They took the whole jrpg grindy repetition thing to an entirely new level by basically recycling the LaD gameplay loops throughout the entire thing though (bottom out, build back up through story content and absurd minigames, run out of story content, still be underleveled, repeat some disconnected dungeon for 20-40 hours, climb tall building to boss...win, start entire game over in ng+) They even recycled the same arena from LaD for the endgame boss... guess Millenium tower is special in ways I cannot fathom. I also felt like they could have done a much better job writing some of the plot twists as they made the main characters into such hopelessly blind fools by the end it was actually cringey and I lost a little respect for a few of them but hey, "they got heart" so... still a fun game.

Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth is a very fun game with a big heart. Story is strong, characters feel real, and gameplay is enjoyable from start to end. Hawaii map also looks nice and full of life. But one thing — game is very long, and later chapters need a lot of level grinding. Some fights feel slow and little annoying. So players who want to buy should know it takes time and patience. If you don’t mind that, the game is really worth it.

Great game. I played the Yakuza: Like A Dragon when it first came out and it was already an amazing game. I've always been into JRPG turn-based style games and this takes it into a new level. I was already expecting this game to be great, but honestly it's even better than the first one! The pace, amount of things to do outside of the main story, and connection with characters feels amazing. I feel deeply involved with the characters and I am very happy to say that the game has been extremely fun. The only downside for me is that I'm spending way too much time playing this game.... (Although some may say that is a good thing)

Would definitely recommend this game to people who have played the first game and love JRPGs.

This is a great game.

As a story/stories: It runs the standard RGG formula complete the same set pieces you've seen a dozen times now, with the added wackiness and optimism you expect from Ichiban. It's not as strong as the previous entry imo, but it's quite good. The B(?) plot is nearly all fanservice for Kiryu enjoyers, and that's fine in its own way. You can skip it easily if it's not what you're here for.

As a JRPG: Combat is greatly improved from the previous Like A Dragon. It's not a system that's going to stress the tactical thinking of any JRPG fans, but it's interesting and flavorful and I didn't get tired of it.

As a collection of Minigames: This game lacks some of my previous favorites, but the collection here is solid, and it makes the smart choice to leave them completely out of your way if you don't vibe with them. No more having to grind out a minigame you dislike for the base weapon of some class's ultimate kit.

Ultimately this shines as a very fun variety pack of strange activities to do and sights to see, and it's very customizable in regards to how much of it you engage with.

I can only recommend this if you've already played Yakuza: Like a Dragon. If you have (and enjoyed it), you'll likely enjoy this one even more thanks to some battle system improvements and pacing adjustments.

A grand, beautiful swan song featuring two larger than life protagonists, Kiryu Kazuma and Ichiban Kasuga. Infinite Wealth marks the end of Kiryu’s journey as well as another monumental adventure for Ichiban and friends. This game is filled to the brim with love for both Kiryu and his character journey as well as inspirational writing for Ichiban’s story. Pair that up incredibly engaging turn based combat, which also rivals and tops the best combat in this series, an impeccable soundtrack, and powerful storytelling and you have the perfect send off package for the Dragon of Dojima.

10/10 An inspiring swan song of life. Thank you RGG

Recommended for fans of turn-based RPGs, Japan, and a good yakuza/redemption story as long as you don't mind some silliness and an abundance of minigames. Too much back and forth with the story that more often than not nothing really meaningful happens. Story interaction with character on Kiryu's side of the story is lackluster compared to Ichiban. Majority of the substories are boring. The RPG elements are just barebone implementation. Jobs are redundant as I see no reason to swap it. I only get to max the main one naturally by the endgame. Weapon upgrade is heavily tied to grind. You'd not have enough to last until the late game without doing so. Even though you can still beat the game with a base weapon, it is still a misopportunity.

I spent the last two days turning some flyover island into a five-star resort, and I've forgotten what the rest of the game is supposed to be about. 10/10. Would pit people against stampeding bulls again.

The good: I can't say enough good about Ichiban being a clueless tourist in Hawaii. Tomizawa and Chitose were great additions, and the majority of the story hooked me. Also loved some of the quality of life improvements to both combat and balancing as that was my biggest gripe with LAD7. The job system feels a lot more open and viable than previously, allowing you to really let any character take any class without feeling like you're punishing yourself. Great character development for both protagonists. The new bond system was also super enjoyable, and the memoirs of a dragon got me teary eyed on more than a few occasions.

The bad: The first 10 hours feel like 75% cutscenes and it takes a while to truly unlock the open world. The game recycles way too many locations, assets, and skills from LAD7. I have nothing against reusing assets or old areas, but a third of the game takes place on the LAD7 map but with less things to explore/discover. I get that it is a sequel, but having only 2 of your 10 party members be new characters is a little insane to me. Sega continuing their legacy of day one DLC that costs way too much money.

Overall: The good far outweighs the bad. If you loved the last game, you're going to love this one.

Even though I must say it didn't have the same emotional impact on me than Yakuza: Like a Dragon did the story was very engaging and left me with watery eyes. Minigames and substories were also fun as always. The only thing that bugged me a little bit was how Saeko was handled here as a character without spoiling too much.
